paragraph: Garfield's volume leader isn't the single-family market, it's two-families. Thirty-two multi-family sales closed at a median of $767,125, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.047 and 78% going above asking in a median of 20 days. Twenty-nine of those 32 were two-family houses, typically five bedrooms and three baths across the units, and that income component is what pushes the price well above the detached market. Single-family is smaller at 21 sales and a median of $565,000, mostly three-bedroom colonials and capes with two baths, and it's competitive on the same terms: 81% sold above asking at a 1.029 ratio in 20 days. Buyers should expect competition on the good ones in both tiers. Condos and townhouses are the quieter category with 10 sales at a median of $525,000, mostly two-bedroom townhouses, a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, and 35 days on market. That tier is where you have room to negotiate. Month to month the counts are too thin to read a trend, so anchor on the six-month medians rather than any single month. If this town follows the usual seasonal arc, expect closings to taper modestly into fall and thin out in deep winter. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor is whether you want the space of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance townhouse.
